You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-f43c759c: Fill gaps between row markers

Colors vary across instances. Identify the row's repeated marker cells (same-color cells distinct from the background); do not hardcode background color. In each row, inspect successive markers from left to right and recolor every background cell strictly between each successive pair to 2. Preserve marker cells and all other cells; do not extend before the first marker or after the last marker, and do not fill across rows. Confirmed palette example: background 4, markers 8, gap-fill 2. Apply independently to every row, including rows with just one marker (no gap to fill).

Evidence: the 13x17 test had background 8 and marker color 0 (not 8). For each row, successive 0 markers delimit background-8 cells to recolor 2; preserve the 0 endpoints and all cells outside those gaps. Rows with fewer than two markers have nothing to fill. A 25x24 demo independently confirmed the same operation with background 1, markers 4, and fill color 2: e.g. a row with markers at columns 7, 9, 11, 13 (0-based) changed only the intervening cells 8, 10, 12; rows with a single marker-free region or fewer than two markers stayed unchanged. This confirms the fill color remains 2 while background and marker colors vary. For a 20x29 recurrence, the rule solved after correcting a manual input transcription; the first failed output had shifted a marker run in one row. Before submitting, validate the copied test grid against the prompt (height, every row width, and coordinates of all non-background markers), then apply the rule mechanically. Colors vary across instances: infer background and marker colors rather than hardcoding them; fill only strictly-between cells and preserve dimensions.
